inputs.share_count_basis: 323.2m shares outstanding at 30 Sep 2026; Q3-2026 10-Q diluted weighted average 323m (dilutive awards immaterial). Held flat because SBC is expensed in the flows.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back, TTM to 30 Sep 2026 = FY2025 91 - 9M-2025 70 + 9M-2026 80 (Q3-2026 10-Q line 2502). No combined equity-award figure is published and no separate net-share-settlement tax line was found; SBC is ~0.3% of revenue so the omission is immaterial.
inputs.fcf_basis_note: reported_fcf and last_fcf are TRAILING TWELVE MONTHS to 30 Sep 2026 (OCF 3,706 = 2,262 - 755 + 2,199; capex 1,292 = 1,878 - 1,428 + 842), levered (after ~480 of interest paid). Neither is a mid-cycle figure: FY2025 owner FCF was 293 (trough, 384 reported less 91 SBC) and the TTM is lifted by Middle East conflict supply constraints and capex cut to ~1.2bn. The model's mid-cycle unlevered owner FCF is ~2.0bn (base, year 5). Interest income (97 in FY2025) is NOT stripped: the company is in net debt, and LYB's EBITDA is struck before all interest.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T21:01:24Z regular close (Friday); valuation run on Sunday 2026-11-15
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is FY2026 ESTIMATED: 9M-2026 actual revenue 24,873 plus a Q4 estimate of ~7,930 (seasonally soft, guided operating rates 85% O&P-Americas / 60% European O&P-EAI / 75% I&D, softer polymer prices after Q3). Year 1 of the projection is FY2027. FY2026 was chosen as FY0 rather than FY2025 because the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet already contains nine months of FY2026 cash flow; projecting FY2026 as year 1 would count ~2bn of it twice (~$6/share). Q4-2026 cash flow (guided seasonal working-capital release) is therefore left out of both the flows and the net debt, a small conservatism of roughly $1-2/share.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.3% (10y UST) + beta ~1.1 x 4.75% ERP = cost of equity ~9.5%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (Nov-2025 issues at 5.125%/5.875%, Baa3/BBB-negative) = ~4.4% after tax; weights ~70/30 on market EV (~20.8bn equity, ~9.1bn net debt) = ~8.0%, rounded up to 8.5% for the sub-investment-grade drift risk in the capital structure. The SAME 8.5% is used in all three scenarios: cyclicality and oversupply risk is charged in the scenario flows and weights, not a second time in the rate (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. US GAAP operating leases: the lease cost is already an operating expense inside reported EBITDA, so lease_cost_pct_path is 0 and operating lease liabilities (1,237 non-current + ~375 current at 30 Sep 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. total_debt 12,331 = current maturities 891 + short-term debt 247 + long-term debt 11,193.
inputs.nci_treatment: Deducted once in the bridge at book: redeemable NCI 114 + NCI 9 (30 Sep 2026). Flows are consolidated; NCI share of income is ~11-12/yr, immaterial.
inputs.equity_affiliate_treatment: Income from equity investments (54 in 9M-2026, ~0 in FY2025, 200-460/yr before 2022) sits INSIDE LYB's segment EBITDA and therefore inside the modelled EBITDA margin; the 3,834 equity-investment carrying value is accordingly NOT added to the bridge (matching-asset rule: in the flows XOR in the bridge). Cash distributions (92 in FY2025) have run close to or above equity income recently, so cash conversion of this line is not a material overstatement at current levels.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical adaptations (owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). LYB is a commodity chemicals operating company - not a bank/REIT/holdco/shell - so the default engine applies; first valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF). MID-CYCLE NORMALISATION IS TWO-SIDED HERE: the brief framed LYB as sitting in a trough, and FY2025 was one (EBITDA ex-impairments ~2.5bn, ~8% margin, net loss, dividend halved Feb-2026). But 9M-2026 is NOT a trough: segment EBITDA was 3,323 reported and ~4,060 before the 734 non-cash loss on the European divestiture, i.e. FY2026E ~5.0bn / ~15% margin, which the Q3-2026 10-Q attributes to Middle East conflict supply constraints, crude/gasoline crack spreads (oxyfuels) and the Bayport PO/TBA restart. Management calls the return to pre-conflict conditions 'non-linear'. The model therefore extrapolates neither year. It anchors the terminal margin on a through-cycle read of continuing-operations EBITDA ex-impairments (refining removed): FY2022 ~14%, FY2023 ~12%, FY2024 ~13.5%, FY2025 ~8%, FY2026E ~15%; five-year average ~12.7%. Base mid-cycle margin 13.5% (credit for exiting loss-making European sites and the Value Enhancement Program), bull 16%, bear 11%. Base path fades FY2026's windfall into a still-oversupplied 2027-2028 (12.0%, 11.5%) before reaching mid-cycle in FY2030. Revenue steps down in FY2027 for conflict-price normalisation and the full-year loss of the four divested European sites (sold May 2026). Working capital is NEGATIVE capture (-12% of revenue change; receivables + inventory less payables ~13-14% of revenue), so a falling top line releases cash and growth consumes it. Cash tax 21% on EBIT (9M-2026 ETR 22.1% incl. a largely non-deductible disposal loss; history 18-21%). Capex: FY2026 budget ~1.2bn (~800 sustaining) under the Cash Improvement Plan is not sustainable in perpetuity; path rises to 4.7% of revenue (~1.5bn), above D&A at 4.5%. Terminal cap 13x mid-cycle owner FCF (cyclical range 12-15x) binds in every scenario (Gordon at 8.5%/2% is 15.7x) and implies ~6x terminal EBITDA. Buybacks: none in 9M-2026 (201 in FY2025; new authorisation of ~34m shares approved May 2026 is unused), so the flat share count is currently a convention the company is not funding - immaterial at 0.3% SBC. Balance-sheet vintage: net debt, shares and NCI at 30 Sep 2026 (Q3-2026 10-Q, filed 30 Oct 2026); pension/OPEB deficit at 31 Dec 2025 (latest actuarial disclosure).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: nominal mid-cycle growth for a mature commodity producer; no trailing CAGR is usable
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All trailing CAGRs end on FY2025, a trough year, and are not usable as a growth anchor. Revenue: FY2022 (50,451) and FY2020 (27,753) include the since-discontinued refining segment while FY2023-FY2025 are recast to continuing operations, so the 3yr figure overstates the decline (like-for-like roughly -8%/yr). EPS: FY2025 is a loss (-2.34), CAGR undefined. Equity: shrunk by ~2.1bn of impairments in 2024-2025 and dividends in excess of earnings. Equity CAGR diverges >30% from revenue.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on owner FCF (reported FCF less SBC; interest income not stripped - net debt): FY2025 293 vs FY2022 4,159 and FY2020 1,402. SBC is ~0.3% of revenue, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs are effectively identical; the collapse is the cycle, not stock comp.

base.narrative: Conflict windfall fades through 2027; oversupply holds margins below mid-cycle through 2028; mid-cycle 13.5% from FY2030.

bull.narrative: Capacity rationalisation and VEP delivery restore a 16% mid-cycle margin by FY2030.

bear.narrative: China-led oversupply is structural; margins revisit FY2025 levels in 2027-2028 and settle at 11%.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026's ~15% EBITDA margin is treated as conflict-aided, not earned. As Middle East supply returns ('non-linear', per management) polymer and oxyfuel spreads normalise into an industry that still has China's ethylene/polyethylene additions to absorb: revenue falls 8% in FY2027 (price normalisation plus a full year without the four divested European sites) and margins sit at 11.5-12% through 2028, consistent with the S&P/Wood Mackenzie/Fitch view that operating rates stay below mid-cycle until 2027-2028. From FY2030 the business earns a 13.5% through-cycle margin - slightly above the 12.7% FY2022-FY2026E average, crediting the exit from loss-making European olefins, the refinery exit and part of the Value Enhancement Program, but far below the 16-20% of 2012-2019. US ethane advantage in O&P-Americas and oxyfuels in I&D carry the earnings; O&P-EAI and APS roughly break even. Capex rises from the 1.2bn austerity budget back to ~1.5bn. Mid-cycle unlevered owner FCF ~2.0bn.
scenario_narratives.bull: The cycle turns earlier and harder: European and high-cost Asian capacity closes at scale by 2027-2028, China's build-out slows, and global operating rates recover while the US ethane/naphtha cost gap stays wide. The Value Enhancement Program reaches its 1.5bn recurring-EBITDA goal by 2028 and actually shows up in reported margins, Bayport and the oxyfuels franchise stay full, and the slimmer European footprint stops diluting the group. Mid-cycle EBITDA margin 16% (~5.5bn) from FY2030 - the level of the better pre-2020 years on the continuing portfolio - with deleveraging restoring mid-BBB credit. Even here the margin is below FY2021's 24% super-peak, which is not treated as repeatable.
scenario_narratives.bear: The oversupply is structural rather than cyclical: China keeps adding self-sufficient olefins and polyolefins capacity and exports the surplus, Middle East supply returns quickly, and the conflict premium in oxyfuels and polyethylene unwinds within a year. Margins revisit FY2025-like levels (9-9.5%) in 2027-2028, revenue falls 12% then 4%, and the 'mid-cycle' the business eventually reaches is only 11%. EBITDA near 2.8bn against 12.3bn of gross debt is ~4.4x, at the edge of the relaxed 4.5x revolver covenant that expires mid-2027, so this path plausibly includes a further dividend cut, a slide to sub-investment grade and more European impairments. Capex is held nearer sustaining levels. The terminal value does not hit the zero floor - the business survives - but equity value is thin after net debt, pension and NCI.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: leverage is real (Baa3, S&P negative outlook, covenant relaxed to 4.5x through mid-2027, dividend already halved) and the oversupply thesis is the consensus industry view, not a tail. Base 50%: a below-mid-cycle 2027-2028 followed by normalisation is what the capacity data and the rating agencies describe. Bull cut to 25%: it needs several independent things - large-scale capacity closures by competitors, VEP benefits surviving as reported margin, and a durable US feedstock gap - to arrive together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A deep cyclical is valued on what it earns across a cycle, not on the year it happens to be in. For LYB that cuts both ways today: FY2025 was a trough and FY2026 is a geopolitically assisted rebound, so the model capitalises a through-cycle 13.5% EBITDA margin (base) on the post-refinery, post-European-divestiture portfolio and lets the scenarios, not the discount rate, carry the uncertainty about where mid-cycle really is. Value is highly levered to that one number: each point of mid-cycle margin is worth roughly $10 per share after 9.1bn of net debt.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin is a judgment, not an observation: the spread between bear (11%) and bull (16%) drives most of the per-share range, amplified by ~9.1bn of net debt plus ~0.95bn of pension and NCI claims.

FY2026E is partly estimated (Q4) and conflict-inflated; if elevated spreads persist longer than modelled, near-term cash flow and deleveraging run ahead of the base case, and vice versa if they snap back.

Capex: the model assumes ~1.5bn/yr (4.7% of revenue) long-run; if the 1.2bn Cash Improvement Plan level proved sustainable value would be roughly $10/share higher, and if deferred turnarounds catch up it is lower.
Terminal value is set by the 13x cap in all scenarios, not by Gordon growth; each turn of the cap is worth roughly $3/share in the base case (12x about -$3, 15x about +$6).
Balance-sheet claims not modelled: environmental/ARO reserves (~200m), PO JV shutdown costs (~215m through 2027), and any residual liabilities from the divested European sites.
Equity-affiliate income is inside EBITDA; a recovery in JV earnings (Saudi, China, Thailand) toward the 300-450/yr of 2017-2021 would be upside the base margin only partly captures.

Hurdle entry prices are very low (bear is negative) because 15% is demanded of a leveraged, low-growth asset: the terminal multiple at a 15% hurdle is ~7.8x rather than 13x and net debt is deducted in full. Read them as 'no 15% return is available here without the bull case', not as a price target.
